clues.title: Bollard: flat post, reflector off-centre
text: Serbia has a few bollard designs, however most of them will have an **off-centred reflector.** The bollards are usually flat, with no depth to them.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Several designs exist, but most are flat posts with the reflector off to one side rather than in the middle. Off-centre reflector is the key.

differs.how: Austrian reflector sits in the centre
Slovenian reflector sits in the centre

clues.title: Guardrail: B-profile (double wave)
text: Serbia uses **B-Profile** guardrails exclusively.
NOTE: North Macedonia does not use B-Profile guardrails. For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/serbia/europeguardrail.png).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Only the B-profile guardrail is used here, the common double-wave shape. North Macedonia does not use it.

differs.how: North Macedonia uses other guardrail profiles

clues.title: Chevron: black arrow on white
text: Serbia uses chevrons with a **black arrow** on a **white** background.
NOTE: Within Europe, these chevrons can also be found in Slovenia, Montenegro and North Macedonia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Curve signs with a black arrow on a white background. Slovenia, Montenegro and North Macedonia use the same look.

clues.title: Plate: white with blue strip on left
text: Serbian licence plates are white with a **blue strip** on the left. Agricultural plates, on vehicles such as tractors, are **green**.
NOTE: Croatian and North Macedonian plates typically do not have a blue strip.

images.caption: Serbian plates: standard white and green agricultural

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White plates with a blue strip on the left. Tractors and farm vehicles have green plates. Croatian and North Macedonian plates usually have no blue strip.

differs.how: Croatian plates usually lack the blue strip
North Macedonian plates usually lack the blue strip

clues.title: Language: Ђ, Ћ in Cyrillic text
text: Serbian is a Slavic language which uses both the **Cyrillic** and Latin script. These letters are unique to Serbian:
- Ђ ђ
- Ћ ћ
These letters are found in Serbian and Macedonian:
- Љ љ
- Њ њ
- Џ џ

images.caption: Serbian Cyrillic text with Ђ and Ћ shown large

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Serbian uses both Cyrillic and Latin script. The letters Ђ and Ћ are only Serbian; Љ, Њ and Џ are shared with Macedonian.

clues.title: Language: Latin letters Č Ć Đ Š Ž
text: When written in the **Latin** script, Serbian uses the special letters Č, Ć, Đ, Š and Ž. Note that all of these letters may also be found in Croatian and Montenegrin.

images.caption: Serbian Latin text with Č Ć Đ Š Ž shown large

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Latin-script Serbian uses Č, Ć, Đ, Š and Ž. Croatian and Montenegrin use all of these letters too.

clues.title: Coverage: four Google car colours
text: Serbia has **4 different truck colours** that were used in different areas.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Four different car colours were used here, each in different areas, so car colour can point to a part of the country.

clues.title: Google car: low-mounted camera, big round blur
text: Serbia also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot. And a short antenna or black blur can be seen on the backside.
NOTE: Most of the Balkans also have Smallcam.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A low-mounted Gen 4 camera with a big round blur, a small bump at the front and a short antenna or black blur at the back. The blur can be see-through, so it is easy to miss. Most Balkan countries have it.

clues.title: Google car: no antenna in Gen 3
text: Most of the Generation 3 coverage in Serbia was taken by a Google car with **no antenna**.
NOTE: Other than North Macedonia, almost all of central and eastern Europe has antenna coverage in Generation 3.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most of the older Gen 3 coverage was shot by a car with no antenna. Almost all neighbouring central and eastern European countries have an antenna in Gen 3, except North Macedonia.

clues.title: Coverage: Gen 3 in north, centre and southeast
text: This is a Generation 3 coverage map of Serbia. Most of the coverage is in the north in Vojvodina, around Belgrade and in the southeast around Niš. Kosovo does not have any Generation 3 coverage.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage is mostly in the north, around the capital and in the southeast. Kosovo has no Gen 3 at all.

clues.title: Landscape: pancake flat plains in the north
text: In the north of Serbia in the Vojvodina region, from the Hungarian border to Belgrade, the landscape is **extremely flat**, with no hills whatsoever. A slight ridge however can be seen at Fruška Gora National Park.

A more hilly landscape can be seen in the central-southern region. The most mountainous regions of Serbia are found in the southwest and southeast, where the Dinaric Alps, Carpathian and Balkan mountains run through Serbia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the far north up to the capital, the land is extremely flat with no hills, apart from one small ridge. Hillier in the centre and south; the highest mountains are in the southwest and southeast.

clues.title: Phone numbers: 2-digit area code, 1 to 3
text: Serbia uses 2 digit area codes, with the first digit **between 1 and 3**. Area codes starting with 2 are found in the north, area codes starting with 1 are found in central and eastern Serbia. Area codes starting with 3 are found in the south-west.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Area codes have 2 digits and the first digit is 1, 2 or 3. 2 is the north, 1 is the centre and east, 3 is the southwest.

clues.title: Landscape: lone low ridge in flat land
text: This slight **ridge** in an otherwise flat landscape can be seen in Fruška Gora National Park, southwest of Novi Sad.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A slight ridge rising from otherwise flat land, in a national park southwest of Novi Sad.

clues.title: Landscape: gentle rolling hills
text: Central-northern Serbia can be recognized by the **slight rolling hills**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the centre-north, slightly rolling hills.

clues.title: Landscape: rolling hills, bigger further south
text: A similarly rolling landscape can be seen in the southern Morava River basin, however **larger hills and mountains** can be seen.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south, a similar rolling landscape along a river basin, but with larger hills and mountains.

clues.title: Landscape: lush green mountains
text: A **lush**, **green**, **mountainous** landscape can be seen in the south and southeast, along the Bulgarian and Kosovo border.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south and southeast, along the Bulgarian and Kosovo borders, the land is lush, green and mountainous.

differs.how: Kosovo looks similar next door, so use borders and signs

clues.title: Coverage: autumn Gen 3 photos
text: Generation 3 **Fall coverage** can be seen in this region south of Čačak, and a small area around Valjevo.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 3 coverage taken in autumn appears south of Čačak and in a small area around Valjevo.

clues.title: Google car: white car, short antenna
text: A white Google Car with a **short antenna** can be seen in Novi Sad, Kovilj, in and around Belgrade, Niš, and the E75 connecting them.
NOTE: The white car is not always visible.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A white Google car with a short antenna shows up around Novi Sad, Belgrade, Niš and the motorway linking them. The car is not always visible.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains rising from flat land
text: The distinct **Vršac Mountains** can be seen east of Vršac near the Romanian border. The mountains protrude out from a flat landscape and [vineyards](https://goo.gl/maps/e2hLdz6HJw4kWN778) can commonly be seen to the south of the mountains. The [Vršac Castle](https://goo.gl/maps/WzaCRBL14QdDEdre7) can also be seen atop the mountain.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Near the Romanian border, a distinct mountain range rises out of flat land, with vineyards to its south and a castle on top.

clues.title: Language: Serbian and Hungarian together
text: **Bilingual signs** with Serbian alongside Hungarian can be seen in northern Vojvodina, where there is a Hungarian majority.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the far north, where many Hungarians live, signs show Serbian next to Hungarian.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: no hat, rounded figure
text: Serbia has 2 different pedestrian signs. **Horizontal Zebra stripe**: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > **No hat + rounded, non-detailed guy**: Serbia. OR **5 Zebra stripes + rounded guy + no belt + white/silver border + no blue corners**: Serbia, and Slovenia.

images.caption: Pedestrian crossing signs compared: Italy, Romania, Serbia and Slovenia

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Two types: a horizontal zebra with a hatless, rounded figure, or five zebra stripes with a rounded figure, no belt and a white or silver border. The second type is shared with Slovenia.

differs.how: Austria's figure is more detailed, has a hat

clues.title: Pole: metal ladder or mesh pole in town
text: Metal poles, either in the shape of a ladder or with a mesh pattern, are common in small town. If you find a random metal pole inside a town, it is probably Serbia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Metal poles shaped like a ladder or with a mesh pattern are common in small towns. A random metal pole inside a town is likely here.

clues.title: Sign: street sign with flag-coloured shield
text: Belgrade street signs have cyrillic and latin written on them, it also has a unique shield icon on the left which has the serbian flag colors in it.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Street signs in the capital show Cyrillic and Latin text and a shield on the left in the national flag colours.
